question: One free-form model call per turn (iteration 1's design A)
why: The core technique (transcript 4:17 to 6:44). It decides the vendor question and the cost.
hypothesis: Fills fastest and is wrong most often.
cost_estimate: about 0.4M Haiku tokens (the test tree's estimate); measured as one free-form call per turn: about 110 on the 20-persona sample and 74 on syn1 per run (the sensitive and instruction turns are never sent)

deviations.from: test tree row: syn2 and real1
deviations.what: Amendment A1 replaces syn2 with anon-personas (kind real, anonymized); Amendment A2 maps the row: every bar the row puts on syn2 applies to anon-personas, and the real1 aggregates (fill_rate_at_k, run_agreement, flips_per_10_turns) are computed on the same anon-personas runs, numbers only, with no extra bar. As a model case it runs the A2 seeded sample of anon-personas, the same one as reverify/heldout-personas: sample_dataset anon-personas, sample_size 20, sample_seed 20261110, random.Random(seed).sample(sorted(user_ids), 20). syn1 stays as the reference, reported beside, never alone.
deviations.cost: Running all 188 personas of anon-personas would cost about 9x the planned budget.
deviations.labels: Labels on anon-personas were written by headless Claude and are not human-reviewed (A2, decision 1): every verdict carries the caveat 'labels not human-reviewed'.
deviations.agg: The row names slot_accuracy twice (mean and min) and outlier_flips pooled; all three apply to anon-personas. 'Pooled' on a count means the three runs' flips added together (lab/core verdict, commit 'a pooled bar on a count adds the runs together'), so at most 1 outlier-caused flip over all three runs together.
deviations.expected_to_fail: The row says 'Expected to fail the second bar'. Its semicolon separates two bars: slot_accuracy (mean and min) and outlier_flips. The second is outlier_flips pooled <= 1, so that bar is marked expected_to_fail: reported, not counted in the verdict. Both slot_accuracy bars count.
deviations.outlier: outlier_flips counts value changes (not first fills) made on a turn tagged 'outlier'. The A1 labels carry such tags on anon-personas (turn ids are strings, '<user_id>-t<N>'; the metric matches them as strings). Realtime has no batch step, so only the turn's own change counts.
deviations.realtime: Strategy realtime (iteration 1's design A): one free-form call per turn on claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 through headless Claude Code, the model rewrites the profile from the current profile and the turn; no thresholds. preferred_language is set by code; a standing instruction is quarantined and never sent. The case pipeline is the replay StrategyPipeline unchanged.
